refactor_baseline.definition: Scientific behavior at this commit is inherited starting state. Only non-structural changes imported after this commit belong in this ledger.

policy.scope: Record every intentional post-baseline algorithm, numerical, default, schema, or scientific-product change imported into the refactor branch.
policy.future_change_rule: Add and validate a ledger entry before accepting a future non-structural change. Link its source, expected effect, affected modes/products, and independent evidence.
policy.baseline_rule: Earlier cleaning and fruit-loop changes already reachable from the refactor baseline are not post-baseline imports and are not relabeled as refactor changes.
policy.comparison_rule: A later OG commit used as a validation comparator is not an imported change unless an integration mapping is recorded here. In particular, ffc6b9070f4744f9778f3db71cdc468846d1da89 is a comparator, not an ancestor or imported commit of this refactor branch.

changes.title: Protect RTC/PTC diagnostic snapshots during parallel scan processing
changes.rationale: Parallel scan workers were reading diagnostic maps and vectors while other workers could still mutate them, producing run-to-run drift. The imported fix takes mutex-protected snapshots and clears caches under the same ownership rules used for writes.

expected_effect.behavior: OpenMP reductions use stable diagnostic snapshots instead of observing concurrently mutating cache state.
expected_effect.numerical_or_schema: No sequential-output or product-schema change is intended. Parallel output should stop drifting run to run and agree with the established sequential point gate under its comparison policy.

validation_evidence.finding: Two byte-identical OMP/6 configurations produced matching manifests, and both matched the protected sequential point baseline after the import.
The current accepted point snapshot retains exact complete-product and timestream behavior with zero unexpected errors.

limitations: The direct run-to-run determinism evidence is the point OMP/6 fixture; other modes are covered by later scientific-equivalence snapshots rather than dedicated repeated-run trials.

changes.title: Reduce Wiener-filter allocation and FFT overhead
changes.rationale: The serial and OpenMP Wiener paths repeatedly allocated FFT outputs and repeated avoidable work in a hot post-processing path. The imported implementation reuses caller-owned buffers, adds bounded denominator controls, and simplifies the OpenMP path.

expected_effect.behavior: Default filtering retains the legacy constant kernel-template tail while reducing transient allocation and redundant FFT work. Optional zero and cosine tail modes intentionally alter the template tail only when explicitly selected.
expected_effect.numerical_or_schema: No default output-schema change is intended. Default filtered products must remain within the pinned mode-specific tolerances; explicitly selecting a non-default tail mode is an intentional filtered-map numerical change.

validation_evidence.finding: The implementation and focused FFT, denominator, convergence, and tail-mode checks are recorded with the legacy-preserving default.
All seven filtered products pass the strict full-Wiener point gate; the simultaneous OG/refactor pair shows no material performance regression.
Twenty-one Wiener-filtered science layers remain within the accepted 1.5% scientific bound while raw maps and diagnostics remain substantially tighter.

limitations: The historical timing pair is operational evidence, not a controlled performance benchmark.
Accepted OOF and Beammap snapshots do not independently exercise every optional Wiener template-tail mode.

changes.title: Restrict PCA covariance solves to active detectors
changes.rationale: The cleaner previously formed and solved a full detector covariance even for flagged or insufficiently sampled detectors. The imported implementation solves only the active subspace and expands the result back to the stable full-detector shape.

expected_effect.behavior: PCA cleaning excludes already flagged detectors and detector columns with fewer than two usable samples from covariance construction, while preserving detector-indexed output shapes.
expected_effect.numerical_or_schema: No product-schema change is intended. Floating-point results may differ slightly because the covariance solve is performed on the active detector subspace; flags, fit stability, and mode-specific products must remain within the accepted scientific contracts.

validation_evidence.finding: The matched Beammap comparison uses the source PCA commit on OG and accepts all detector flags, map layers, sensitivities, positions, and beam widths under the versioned scientific profile.
The science comparison retains exact integer diagnostics and very small accepted map, PTC-weight, detector-median, and other diagnostic differences.
The current accepted point snapshot retains exact complete-product and timestream behavior across the later structural work.

limitations: The import intentionally changes the numerical route for flagged-detector cases, so equivalence is scientific and contract-based rather than a claim of universal bitwise identity.
